subject: Chemistry
title: Protein Structural Hierarchy (1°, 2°, 3°, 4°) & Denaturation
topics: 6. Protein Structural Hierarchy Overview (Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, Quaternary)
6.1 Primary (1°: Linear Peptide Sequence), Secondary (2°: α-Helix & β-Pleated Sheets via Backbone H-Bonds)
Tertiary (3°: 3D Spatial Folding via Disulfide -S-S-, Salt Bridges, Hydrophobic Forces)
Quaternary (4°: Multi-Subunit Arrangement e.g., Hemoglobin α₂β₂ Tetramer)
6.2 Denaturation: Destruction of 2°, 3°, 4° Structures Leaving 1° Covalent Peptide Sequence COMPLETELY INTACT
quickSummary: Proteins have 4 structural levels: 1° (covalent peptide sequence), 2° (α-helix and β-pleated sheets via backbone H-bonds), 3° (3D globular folding via disulfide -S-S-, salt bridges, hydrophobic forces), and 4° (oligomeric subunit assembly). Denaturation destroys 2°, 3°, and 4° structures, causing loss of biological activity, but leaves PRIMARY STRUCTURE (1° peptide bonds) COMPLETELY INTACT.
summary: Master protein structural hierarchy and denaturation mechanisms.

summaryBox.title: Protein Folding Hierarchy
summaryBox.takeaway: 1°: Peptide sequence. 2°: Backbone H-bonds (α-helix, β-sheet). 3°: 3D folding (-S-S-, salt bridges, hydrophobic). 4°: Subunit assembly (Hb α₂β₂).

PROTEIN STRUCTURAL HIERARCHY
                                     │
     ┌───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
     ▼                               ▼                               ▼
PRIMARY STRUCTURE ($1^\circ$)   SECONDARY STRUCTURE ($2^\circ$) TERTIARY STRUCTURE ($3^\circ$)
Linear amino acid sequence      Local backbone folding          3D spatial folding
linked by peptide bonds.        stabilized by H-bonds.          stabilized by hydrophobic,

conceptBreakdown.heading: 6.2 Denaturation of Proteins
conceptBreakdown.title: 6.2 Denaturation of Proteins
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
DENATURATION EFFECTS
                            
   Native Active Globular Protein ──[Heat / pH Change]──► Unfolded Inactive Polypeptide
   
   * CRITICAL NEST TRAP: Denaturation destroys $2^\circ, 3^\circ,$ and $4^\circ$ structures,
     BUT leaves the **PRIMARY STRUCTURE ($1^\circ$ covalent peptide bonds) COMPLETELY INTACT**!
   * Examples: Coagulation of egg white albumins upon boiling; Curdling of milk (lactic acid denatures casein).
conceptBreakdown.content: Denaturation unfolds the secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structures due to disruption of non-covalent interactions, but does NOT cleave covalent peptide bonds.

quickRevision: Primary (1°): amino acid sequence held by covalent peptide bonds.
Secondary (2°): α-helix and β-sheet held by backbone H-bonds.
Tertiary (3°): 3D folding held by -S-S-, salt bridges, hydrophobic forces.
Quaternary (4°): spatial arrangement of multiple subunits (Hb α₂β₂).
PRIMARY STRUCTURE (1° peptide bonds) REMAINS INTACT during denaturation.
